A1.justification: The PDFs describe the same work, renamed from OrionBench to InfoDet, with matching construction methods and three principal applications. Both main texts and complete appendices, including figures and tables, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ChartQAPro experiments, detector evaluations, prompting and dataset-composition ablations, and transfer experiments on Rico and DocGenome.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical evaluations and additionally reports mark-level detection, cross-dataset transfer, dataset-quality analyses, and additional pre-training controls.

M1.justification: The InternImage-L/DINO annotation loop and Thinking-with-Boxes procedure remain intact. The construction procedure changes from Pinterest-led snowballing to reported manual collection from selected platforms, and v4 explicitly extends synthetic generation and annotation to produce 26 mark categories.

E1.justification: v4 adds mark-level detection of chart sub-elements and bidirectional transfer evaluation with VG-DCU, substantially extending task coverage beyond chart/HRO detection. The real-image source mix also changes, including removal of Pinterest and addition of sources such as OECD. ChartQAPro, Rico, and DocGenome remain.

E2.justification: The eleven detection models and three ChartQAPro prompting baselines are retained. The layout-detection comparison expands from two pre-training variants in v1 Table 4 to four in v4 Table 5, adding no-pre-training and InfoDet-only controls.

E3.justification: The reported dataset changes from 26,250 real and 78,750 synthetic images to 11,264 real and 90,000 synthetic images; training size changes from 100,000 to 96,264, while testing remains 5,000 with the revised mixture. New protocols include transfer over four shared mark categories and a 500-image synthetic-quality audit. Existing fine-tuning hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1's training-size and real/synthetic-mixture ablation is removed from both the main text and supplement. v4 adds diversity, bias, synthetic-quality and feature-space coverage analyses in Appendix F, cross-dataset generalization tests in Appendix I, and additional pre-training controls. The prompting ablations and o3 error analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-run detector averages and standard deviations, with exceptions for the paid T-Rex2 and DINO-X APIs. The new mark-level results follow the existing repeated-run reporting practice. No new confidence intervals, significance tests, or seed-control procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: Detector results are extensively replaced: Table 3 reports Co-DETR chart/HRO AP of 90.1/86.0 in v1 and 88.2/64.0 in v4. These concern revised datasets, not a same-setting decline. v4 adds mark-level, transfer, quality-audit and pre-training-control results, including Co-DETR mark-level mAP of 69.6. ChartQAPro Table 1 remains numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results, assumptions, proofs, or mathematical derivations. The added PMI and feature-space coverage analyses are empirical evaluation procedures rather than new theoretical developments.

C1.justification: The central resource contribution expands from chart/HRO detection to infographic-element detection including finer-grained chart marks. An annotation extension presented as future work in v1's conclusion becomes a delivered contribution in v4's introduction and conclusion. The three principal application claims remain.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations concerning stronger transfer from infographic training, synthetic representativeness, diversity, and absence of harmful bias. It also discusses distinctive real versus synthetic chart characteristics. The interpretation that mixing real and synthetic data avoids performance saturation disappears with its ablation; the real-image fine-grained classification limitation remains.

D1.justification: v4 adds the 26-label mark vocabulary, Gemini-based attribute-analysis details, CLIP/UMAP audit procedures, explicit platform licenses, and a statement that real images are distributed through source URLs only. Existing prompts, optimizer settings, hardware and training-time disclosures are largely retained.

R1.justification: The plain-chart versus infographic positioning remains. v4 adds VG-DCU, ChartGalaxy and InfoChartQA, attributes template-based generation to ChartGalaxy, and supplies a comparative dataset table. Some earlier references, including RefChartQA and the snowballing and performance-scaling sources, disappear.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming the work, v4 substantially reorganizes the document: it removes the NeurIPS checklist, integrates the separately titled supplement into continuous appendices, consolidates references, and moves ethics into the main document. Collection and results passages are also rewritten, although the main section sequence remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v4 redraws the collection pipeline and dataset histograms, adds a coverage heatmap and tables for mark detection, dataset comparison, diversity and transfer, and expands the layout-detection table. The size/mix plots and chart/HRO-category treemaps disappear. Conference formatting also changes figure placement, typography and page layout throughout.

improvement.justification: The new transfer tests and no-pre-training/InfoDet-only controls strengthen evidence for dataset usefulness, while quality audits and licensing details improve documentation. However, removing the size/mix ablation loses evidence about combining data sources, and Appendix J's restricted LLM-use statement conflicts with the generation and audit descriptions. These tradeoffs support a limited net improvement.
